one_month_reasoning: Oracle's Q2 FY27 results are set for 2026-12-14, outside the window. Inside 2026-10-05..11-04: (1) the $0.50 dividend goes ex around the Oct 9 record date, mechanically lowering the price ~$0.50; (2) the October Investor Day promised on the Q1 call (likely around AI World, Oct 25-28), where management deferred AI-infrastructure gross-margin detail and may or may not give an FCF-positive date - a two-sided guidance event (a credible FCF date or FY30 targets would be a positive; another 'no time frame' plus higher capex would be negative); (3) Big-4 Q3 prints and 2027 capex guides in late October and the FOMC Oct 27-28; (4) fresh skeptic attention (Burry's early-October note on prepayment-financed backlog) which is already public on Oct 5. No new bonds are planned in CY2026 and the ATM is exhausted, so near-term supply of stock is lower than I assumed in round 1; the Jan-May 2027 financing is outside the window. Moody's (Baa2 negative) could act at any time but S&P is stable, so a junk cut inside a month is unlikely. I therefore centre a lognormal at ~$142.4 (spot less the dividend, no drift view) with monthly sigma ~15% plus a 15% weight on a wider (27%) component for the Investor Day, giving effective vol slightly above the 16% (56%/3.5) quiet-month baseline.

fair_value.method: Blend of 0.6 x forward P/E (Oct-2027 NTM EPS: consensus-implied $12.33 cut by one labelled 15% skeptic haircut to $10.48, x 14x = ~$147) and 0.4 x skeptic DCF valued at Oct-2027 (~$115 after ~$135B horizon net debt and 3.16B shares) = ~$134.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Oct-2027 NTM (Oct-27..Sep-28 = 8/12 FY28 + 4/12 FY29) consensus-implied EPS = 8/12 x $11.00 + 4/12 x ~$15.0 = $12.33; one labelled skeptic haircut of 15% (i.e. I am 15% below the street) -> $10.48; x 14x (inside peer range, below 21.6x median) = $146.8

inputs_detail.derivation: Yahoo/StockAnalysis consensus; matches the Q1 FY27 release guide. Used for CY2027 comps only.

No non-GAAP FY29 consensus is published. Zacks GAAP-like basis: FY28 $9.14, FY29 $12.84 (only 5 estimates). Applying the ratio 1.40 to $11.00 gives $15.45 (supervisor figure, verified); I instead carry the GAAP-to-non-GAAP gap forward additively (gap $1.45 FY27, $1.86 FY28, ~$2.2 FY29), giving ~$15.0, because SBC/amortization grow more slowly than earnings so GAAP growth overstates non-GAAP growth.

8/12 x $11.00 + 4/12 x $15.0 (FY28 runs Jun-27..May-28, so 8 of the NTM months fall in FY28). Replaces round-1 CY2028 basis with an FY29 input that was itself below consensus (the double haircut the supervisor flagged).

Applied once, to consensus. Components: ~4-5% dilution (3,023.7M shares at 2026-09-07; ~$20-40B of further debt/equity expected Jan-May 2027 on a ~$40B FY27 plan; 6.50% Series D mandatory convertible); ~4% higher interest cost (Q1 interest expense ~$1.4B, +55% y/y; S&P sees FY27 FOCF ~-$42B); ~4% OCI margin/ramp risk (AI-infra GM 30-40%, Jupiter force majeure and permit delays); ~3% earnings-quality risk (FY29 consensus rests on 5 estimates; ASC 606 financing component on $11.4B prepayments flagged by Burry inflates later revenue vs cash). I am therefore ~15% below the street on NTM EPS, stated plainly.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Valued at Oct-2027: FCF rest-of-FY28 -$10B, FY29 $0, FY30 +$15B, FY31 +$30B; terminal 18x on normalized ~$37B FCF (FY31 revenue ~$220B x ~17%); 10% discount rate -> EV ~$497B; less ~$135B horizon net debt (notes + finance leases - cash; operating leases excluded) = ~$362B / 3.16B shares = ~$115

I take management's ~100% post-tax-EBITDA-to-FCF conversion claim seriously only for completed projects before reinvestment: GPUs depreciate over ~5-6 years and must be replaced, so the steady-state cloud margin is far below project-level conversion.
Management calls FY27-28 peak capex years with no FCF-positive date; capex CY2027 ~$110B base per the standing capex view; prepayments and bring-your-own-hardware narrow the deficit
Equity cost above large-cap norm given BBB-/Baa2-negative credit and 6.4-8% long bond yields; 18x FCF ~5.5% FCF yield
3,023.7M at 2026-09-07 + ~100M from ~$15B of equity at ~$140 + ~35M from the mandatory convertible

bear.story: OpenAI cannot fund its compute bill and stretches or restructures the Oracle contract; RPO conversion slips, Jupiter and other sites delayed; Moody's cuts to Baa3 and S&P moves to negative or junk, financing costs jump and the Jan-May 2027 raise is mostly equity at low prices. NTM EPS ~$9 on more shares, market pays ~9.5x.

base.story: OCI grows strongly (RPO converts roughly on schedule) but FCF stays negative through FY28; ~$20-40B more debt/equity in early 2027; S&P stays BBB- stable, Moody's negative. The stock trades ~13x my haircut NTM EPS of ~$10.5 (~11x consensus), i.e. between my P/E leg ($147) and DCF ($115).

bull.story: AI demand holds (hyperscaler 2027 capex guides up again), the Investor Day gives a credible FCF-positive date and 35-40% OCI margins, prepayments and BYOH cut net capex, spreads tighten and an OpenAI IPO/funding round derisks the counterparty; rerates to ~17x on consensus NTM ~$12.3.

comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount, argued as persistent through Oct-2027 on company facts, not sell-side calls: (1) management calls FY27-28 the peak capex years and declined to give an FCF-positive date (Q1 call), so FCF stays negative through May 2028 while every peer self-funds; (2) S&P BBB- (stable) and Moody's Baa2 (negative), one notch from junk at S&P, while the hyperscaler peers are A or better; ~$20-40B more financing is due Jan-May 2027; (3) ~half of the $664B RPO is one loss-making counterparty (S&P); (4) non-GAAP EPS is ~23% above GAAP (Q1 $1.92 vs $1.56) and prepayments carry an ASC 606 financing component, so earnings quality is below the near-GAAP hyperscalers. Against that ORCL has the fastest EPS growth in the set (+35% FY28), which is why I stop at the lower quartile rather than going below the range. Moving to the median needs FCF visibility - that is my bull case, not the base.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$95 (~10.4x current NTM consensus EPS of ~$9.1, ~7.7x Oct-2027 consensus NTM) the market would be pricing a fundamental break rather than volatility: a junk rating (now needing S&P to abandon its stable outlook, or a two-notch Moody's move), an OpenAI contract restructuring/cancellation, or an equity raise large enough to impair per-share earnings. I keep $95 rather than the supervisor's ~$100 because the 52-week low ($114.50) and 56% vol make $100 reachable on sentiment alone; $95 is ~17% below my DCF ($115) and ~17% below the 52-week low, so reaching it needs new bad news, not just drift.

reasoning: Skeptic lane, round 2. Supervisor corrections accepted after verification: S&P is BBB- with a STABLE outlook (heise, Jul 2026) and only Moody's Baa2 is negative, so the junk tail is a bit thinner; the Q2 EPS guide is $1.85-1.93 USD ($1.83-1.91 cc) (8-K Ex.99.1); net debt is $88.2B incl. $0.7B securities; an Investor Day is promised for October (transcript); Q2 reports Dec 14; and my round-1 P/E leg double-haircut (FY29 $13.75 already below consensus, then -16%). I verified the Zacks FY29/FY28 ratio (12.84/9.14 on 5 estimates) and use ~$15.0 non-GAAP FY29 (additive GAAP gap, slightly below the supervisor's $15.4). New skeptic evidence: Burry (Oct 2026) argues the backlog is prepayment-financed with ASC 606 financing components - an earnings-quality point I fold into one labelled 15% haircut. Valuation: NTM Oct-27..Sep-28 consensus-implied $12.33 -> $10.48 after haircut x 14x (lower quartile of a 10-peer CY27 median of 21.6x, range 8.5-27x; discount argued persistent) = $147; DCF at Oct-2027 with ~17% normalized FCF margin (up from 15% after weighing management's project-level 100% EBITDA-to-FCF claim against GPU refresh), 10%/18x, ~$135B horizon net debt, 3.16B shares = $115; blend 60/40 = $134 (from $129). Scenarios: bear $85 (27%), base $138 (50%), bull $212 (23%), mean $140.7; the ~$7 gap to fair value is the right skew (bull +$74 vs bear -$53) and the base case sitting nearer the P/E leg, since the market prices ORCL on multiples within 12 months while my DCF is more punitive. The ladder is a lognormal mixture on those scenarios (sigmas 0.35/0.25/0.27): median ~$137, P(>=143) 0.45, P(>=100) 0.77, P(>=215) 0.13; versus round 1 the middle is slightly lower because I aligned the base case with fair value, while the left tail is thinner (S&P stable). Research limited to ~8 follow-up checks; EV/EBITDA comps not collected.
